**The owner's homepage, desktop AND mobile, as ONE layout with zero media queries.** Ten bands, built separately then assembled. `scrollWidth === clientWidth` at 400 / 1280 / 1920 / 3440 on both urls — 8/8, zero console errors.

![](shots/exhibit.png)

**The claim — *".flex.auto etc makes it pretty easy"* — holds, with one named exception.** All 24 flex and grid seams are one line at 1280+ and two or more at 400. Three words do the whole transition: `flex auto gap` + a `--column` basis for every two-track band, `grid auto gap` for every wall (`auto-fit` caps the columns at the card count, so three cards can never become four at 3440), and source order instead of `reverse`. The exception is the nav, which needs `flex: 1 1 22em` and has no word for it.

REOPENED by the mastermind — a defect the acceptance test structurally could not see. At 1440: 4549px of content inside a 284px .flex-1 (16.0x), seven of ten bands unreachable, document not scrolling. scrollWidth === clientWidth is HORIZONTAL only, and the page heights I reported were the inner scroller's, not the document's. Both numbers were true.

VERDICT — `fill` is wrong for any content-heavy page, and that is a tier finding, not a bug in mine. `fill` claims one screen and hands the scroll to one pane: right for an app shell, wrong for a document. landing/document/hero share the identical string and are clean only because their demo bands fit a viewport — each is one longer demo away from this. Now `page full flex v`, no flex-1, no overflow-y.

FIXED and re-verified at 400/1280/1440/1920/3440 — page 9713/5043/5094/5544/6235 against a 1000px client, zero inner scrollers, scrollWidth === clientWidth at all five, zero console errors. Before/after at 1440: 16.0x -> 1.0x.

--grow fix confirmed: retuned to the Figma's own seams and measured EXACTLY 1.40 and 0.80 at 1280/1440/1920/3440 (comp: 1.40 and 0.78). Gotcha found on the way — the basis scales with the weight now, so a weight moves the WRAP THRESHOLD: `4`/`5` for a 0.8 seam stacked at every width. Express weights near 1.

Cost of the fix, stated: the card shows the masthead instead of a pinned footer. Re-locking it would re-create the porthole in miniature (~440px holding 4500px at 56em). A card is a picture; a picture of a long page is its top.

assign.outcome:
**The owner's homepage, desktop AND mobile, as ONE layout with zero media queries — and the viewport-lock defect found on review is fixed.** Ten bands. Verified at 400 / 1280 / **1440** / 1920 / 3440 on both axes: `scrollWidth === clientWidth` at all five, **no internal scroller anywhere**, zero console errors.

![](shots/home-1440.png)

**The defect, and why it is a finding about the tier.** Shipped as `page full fill flex v` — the string `landing`, `document` and `hero` all use. At 1440 that gave the middle region **284px to hold 4549px (16.0x)**: seven of ten bands in the DOM and unreachable, with no horizontal symptom and nothing thrown. The string was not the culprit; **content volume** was. `fill` is a claim that a layout *fits one screen* and hands the scroll to one pane — right for an app shell (`shell`, `mail`, `chat`, `dashboard`, `split`), wrong for a document. **A marketing homepage wants document scroll.** Now `page full flex v`, no `flex-1`, no `overflow-y`. Before/after at 1440: **16.0x → 1.0x**, page height 5094 against a 1000px client.

`landing`, `document`, `docs` and `stack` all wear `fill` today and none is broken — because none holds enough content to collapse. **Each is one longer demo away from this.**

**Why the first test missed it, now a line in the `layout` skill.** `scrollWidth === clientWidth` is horizontal only, and on a `fill` page the "page height" you naturally reach for is the *inner scroller's* `scrollHeight` — both numbers read healthy while the page was unusable. Assert `inner.scrollHeight <= inner.clientHeight + 50` on every `overflow-y: auto` box, and **test 1440**. (`fullPage` screenshots are blind here too: `.layout-full` is `position: fixed; overflow: auto`, so the document is always one viewport tall.)

**`--grow` confirmed fixed, with one broadcast.** Retuned to the comp's own seams and measured **exactly 1.40 and 0.80** at 1280 / 1440 / 1920 / 3440 (Figma: 1.40 and 0.78), flat. ⚠ The basis scales with the weight now, so a weight also moves the **wrap threshold** — `4`/`5` for a 0.8 seam stacked at *every* width. Express weights near 1, not as the smallest integer pair.

**Findings #2 and #3 stand** (`.wash`/`.tint` keyed to colour-scheme; no word for a fluid child with a real basis on a plain wrapping row). **Cost of the fix:** the card shows the masthead rather than a pinned footer — re-locking it re-creates the porthole in miniature. **Left:** the duplicate `Services-Section` (string recorded, not built), placeholders for pictures and social marks, and three mobile-only moves that ship as the desktop reading rather than adding the page's first `@media`.
